chunks: Abu Abdillah al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa', from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) sat in the posture of 'mutawarrika', his right leg upon his left thigh. So a man said to him, 'May I be your ransom, this is an abhorrent sitting posture.'

He said, 'No, but rather it is something which the Jews say: when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was finished from creating the heavens and the earth and Established Himself upon the Throne, He sat in this posture to rest.'
Allah is He besides Whom there is no god, the Everliving, the Eternal; slumber does not seize Him nor sleep
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) remained sitting in the 'mutawarrika' posture just as he was.

key_terms.الْيَهُودُ: The Jews (referenced here for their interpretation of divine attributes)
key_terms.جِلْسَةٌ مَكْرُوهَةٌ: An abhorrent or disliked sitting posture
key_terms.مُتَوَرِّكاً: A sitting posture where one leg is placed across the thigh

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the 'mutawarrika' sitting posture and its theological significance?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defends the 'mutawarrika' sitting posture against critics who deemed it abhorrent, linking it to a Jewish interpretation of divine rest after creation. By citing Ayat al-Kursi, the Imam clarifies that while Allah 'sat' (istawa) on the Throne, it was not due to physical fatigue or sleep, thereby validating the posture as a sign of dignified ease rather than exhaustion. This highlights the Shia scholarly approach of using Quranic exegesis to justify Prophetic and Imamic customs (Sunnah) against cultural misconceptions.

en.hubeali: Abu Abdullah Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Hammad Bin Usman who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws sat ‘Mutawarrika’, hisasws right leg being upon hisasws left thigh. So a man said to himasws, ‘This is an abhorrent sitting posture’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. But rather, it is a thing which the Jews say that when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic was free from Creating the skies and the earth and Established upon the Throne, Sat in this posture in order to rest.
So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Revealed [2:255] Allah is He besides Whom there is no god, the Everliving, the Eternal; slumber does not seize Him nor sleep
, and Abu Abdullahasws remained sitting ‘Mutawarrika’ posture just as heasws was’.
en.sarwar: 5. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Mu’ Alla ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman who has said the following: “
Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) was sitting with his right foot on his left thigh. A man said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, this sitting posture is not desirable.’

The Imam said, ‘It is not so. That is a thing the Jews say that when Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, finished creating the heavens and earth and took His place on the Throne, He sat in this posture to rest and relax.

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, revealed 255 of Chapter 2 of the Holy Quran, “Allah exists. No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, the Everlasting and the Guardian of life. Drowsiness or sleep does not seize him. . . .’” [2:255]
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) continued to remain in that sitting posture.’”
